Facts:
- Howard University Hospital was established in 1862 in Washington, D.C., to serve thousands of African Americans who came to the city during the Civil War seeking freedom.
- Howard University Hospital, previously known as Freedmen's Hospital, was the first hospital of its kind to provide medical treatment for former slaves.
- Howard University Hospital later became the major hospital for the Washington, D.C., area's African American community and has served that community for over 150 years.
- The Psychiatric Institute of Washington opened in 1967 in Washington, D.C., as a short-term private psychiatric hospital.
- The Psychiatric Institute of Washington is an acute 104-bed psychiatric hospital in Washington, D.C.
- Howard University Hospital is a major hospital in Washington, D.C., built on the site of the former Griffith Stadium.
